failures.cause: GCP projects now default to OS Login enabled at project level; instance metadata SSH keys are ignored. Instance-level enable-oslogin=FALSE + reset didn't override project-level policy fast enough
failures.resolution: bypass: use gcloud compute ssh (OS Login path) to append public key to user's authorized_keys directly

failures.cause: user pasted ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine private key contents into conversation
failures.resolution: user asked to rotate key when convenient; Cipher refused to use leaked key

lessons: Bake `enable-oslogin=FALSE` into BOTH instance and project metadata at create time in future cycles — don't fight it mid-migration.
Better: provision new VM with gcloud compute ssh --command='...' to append Cipher's pubkey directly to the OS Login user. No metadata SSH-keys needed at all.
Never paste private keys in chat. Use gcloud compute ssh and inject our public key to the existing OS Login user.
